title: The Halvorsen Bequest
tagline: A death in a cold store, filed as an accident. Is it?
hook: A conservator is found dead in a refrigerated art vault. He had a heart condition, a written exemption barring him from that room, and he went in anyway without his monitor. The Medical Examiner recorded accidental death and the file closed in eleven days. Six weeks later the insurers refused the claim. You are the review team.
note: Start here. This case teaches the whole system.
advice: Every one of these was suggested by something already in the file. Before you spend, ask what in the closed file made you want it - and if you cannot answer, spend it on something you can answer for.

persons.label: Eliminations
persons.hint: A suspect is eliminated only when a document places them beyond the act, and only against the time of death you have established - not the one you were handed.

exhibits.name: Personal oxygen monitor, Meridian issue, unit 06
exhibits.found: Charging cradle, B2 anteroom - fully charged, not deployed

exhibits.name: Tablet computer, carried by the deceased at all times
exhibits.found: Not in Cold Store 3, the B2 anteroom, the conservation lab, his office, his vehicle or his home

motiveLabel: Motive (optional - scores nothing, but the file is thin without it)

accusation.question: On the evidence recorded, the death of Tobias Renn was...

options.label: An accident
options.sub: The original finding stands. Nobody is named.

options.label: Unlawful killing by Dr Lena Kovaleski

phases.prompt: Write down your working time of death, and which suspects are plausible.

phases.read: the four interviews (C-1 to C-4) and D-1
phases.prompt: Revise both in writing: your time of death, and your plausible suspects. Authorities are now open.

rules: The documents don't lie. People might. Every untruth in the transcripts can be caught by a document. If a statement and a log disagree, the log is right.
The whole file is yours. The tension is in what you spend, not what you hide.
You have a fixed number of Authorities and they do not come back. Not every one returns something useful. Before you spend, say out loud what in the file made you want it.
Write your working on the Resolution Sheet as you establish it, with document references. Anything not written before the final accusation scores nothing.
You get two wrong accusations. Each costs 10 points and opens a Reconsider envelope naming the gap in your theory. The third accusation is final.
When you are done, sign the sheet and break the seal on Envelope S-1. Read it aloud, in order.

printKit.envelopes: 15 envelopes: 11 numbered 01-11, 3 marked RECONSIDER, 1 marked S-1

files.name: 01 Base dossier
files.what: The case file. Everyone reads all of it. Leave it loose on the table.

files.name: 02 Play materials
files.what: Briefing, Authority menu, Case Resolution Sheet. One set per table.

files.name: 03 Authority results
files.what: Separate without reading. One page per envelope, numbered 01-11.

files.name: 04 Reconsider and Envelope S-1
files.what: Pages 1-3 seal separately (Reconsider). Pages 4-8 seal together (S-1).

checklist: Print the Player pack (single-sided is best, so pages can lie side by side)
Print spares of B-1 page 2 and both D-1 pages for 2+ players
Someone who is NOT playing prints the Sealed pack face-down
Put Authority results 01-11 in 11 numbered envelopes, one page each, unread
Seal the 3 Reconsider inserts separately (Pryce, Kovaleski, Ferraro)
Seal the 5 pages of Envelope S-1 together, cover facing out
Put S-1 out of casual reach, and find two pencils

hints.q: When did Tobias Renn really die?
steps: The autopsy did its arithmetic perfectly. Check the inputs it was given, and where each one was measured.
Compare where the ambient temperature was taken (A-1, Scene Conditions) with the temperature of the room he lay in all evening (D-1, section 2).
Use Appendix M in B-1. At 6 °C the multiplier is 1.94, so the elapsed interval is 5.0 ÷ 1.94 hours. Work the time forward from 00:41.
A room held at 15% oxygen does not fall further on its own. Something in the file is counting events.
D-1 section 3 says the life-safety controller logged two discrete events, and the full log is not in the extract.
Spend Authority 11 and read the interlock lines closely.
Whoever did it needed a particular kind of access to the suppression system.
E-1.1 lists who can override the occupancy interlock. There are very few names.
Only two people hold Level 4. Test the alibi of one (Authority 08) and the route of the other (Authorities 01 and 03).

hints.q: How do I clear a suspect?
steps: A suspect is cleared only against the time of death you have established, not the one printed in the file.
Ferraro is the easy one: E-1.2. Kovaleski badged out of B2 at 21:26 (D-1 section 1), which only clears her if he died later than that.
Pryce needs three records together: his checkpoint scans (Authority 03), the discharge time (Authority 11) and the freight lift log (Authority 01).
Every useful Authority is pointed at by something already in the file. D-1 section 5 lists what the extract left out.
Some add nothing new: a second toxicology panel will not change the cause of death, and corroborating an alibi you already hold is a luxury.
The decisive four are 11, 01, 03 and 08. Authority 06 supplies the motive.
